title: No Free Lunch: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Undermines Fairness in LLMs, Even for Vigilant Users
findings: The 'Religion' bias category was found to be a 'Vulnerable Category', meaning its fairness is significantly degraded when RAG retrieves biased data from other categories. The study demonstrated a significant drop in fairness for this category when RAG used uncensored data. Furthermore, even when using a fully censored, 'clean' external dataset, RAG still compromised fairness in the religion category compared to not using RAG at all.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures the introduction or amplification of social biases in LLM outputs when using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). For religion, this specifically involves measuring stereotypical bias in question-answering tasks (from the BBQ dataset) and toxicity in generated text following prompts related to religious identity (from the HolisticBias dataset).
